cards.front: [ CRISPR/Cas9 ] is a genome editing tool that is derived from bacteria to knock in / out any DNA sequence
cards.raw0: {{c1::CRISPR/Cas9}} is a genome editing tool that is derived from bacteria to knock in / out any DNA sequence
cards.back: - This utilizes variants of the Cas9 endonuclease to introduce either a single or double strand break to allow for the insertion of DNA constructs or removal of target DNA sequences - The entire system (Cas9 + gRNA) is typically encoded into a plasmid which is delivered to target cells via electroporation (allows for easy transfection of plasmid into target cell) or viral systems (e.g., adenovirus / lentivirus; used for hard to transfect cells e.g., stem cells) [img] Photo credit: marius walter , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: At its core, CRISPR/Cas9 utilizes an endonuclease ([Cas9]) and a(n) [ guide ] RNA that binds to a complementary target DNA sequence
cards.raw0: At its core, CRISPR/Cas9 utilizes an endonuclease ({{c2::Cas9}}) and a(n) {{c1::guide}} RNA that binds to a complementary target DNA sequence
cards.back: - Guide RNA ( gRNA ) is contained inside of a "crRNA", which along with "tracrRNA" forms the active "sgRNA" which will target the sequence; multiple crRNA's can be combined (to insert more DNA) - The gRNA can be designed to target ANY DNA sequence, which brings the endonuclease to that site to introduce a gap ; PAM sequences are sites where Cas9 can bind [img] Photo credit: marius walter , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: When using CRISPR/Cas9 that introduce a double strand break to knock-out target DNA, [nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) enzymes] repair the gap introduced by this Cas9 variant
cards.raw0: When using CRISPR/Cas9 that introduce a double strand break to knock-out target DNA, {{c1::nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ) enzymes}} repair the gap introduced by this Cas9 variant
cards.back: However, the use of a Cas9 variant that permits single stranded breaks (when spaced properly) can trigger homology directed repair (less error prone) [img] Photo credit: marius walter , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

cards.front: When using CRISPR/Cas9 to knock-in DNA, a(n) [repair template] must be added to guide insertion of a construct
cards.raw0: When using CRISPR/Cas9 to knock-in DNA, a(n) {{c1::repair template}} must be added to guide insertion of a construct
cards.back: Ideally, you use a Cas9 variant that introduces a single stranded break that would allow Homology Directed Repair to utilize the provided repair template to incorporate the new sequence into the target cells genome [img] Photo credit: marius walter , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons
